title: Plain paratha
subtitle: Flaky layered Indian flatbread made by folding fat into the dough during rolling
excerpt: A paratha folds fat into the dough during rolling to create flaky, separated layers. Roll, spread with ghee, fold, rest, roll again. The technique takes about ten minutes of active work but produces a much softer and more layered result than a single-stage flatbread.
sourceNotes: Paratha is a staple flatbread across India and Pakistan, particularly at breakfast. The basic plain (sada) paratha is the foundational form from which stuffed, multi-layered, and enriched versions derive. The technique of rolling, adding fat, folding, and re-rolling to create layers is consistent across the published Indian cookery literature.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooked, cooled parathas with baking paper between each. Reheat from frozen in a dry pan for 1 minute per side.
recipe.batchNotes: Scale the dough in proportion. Rest time does not increase with larger batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dough can be made up to 1 day ahead and kept covered in the fridge. Bring to room temperature before rolling.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Cooked on a dry tawa, cast-iron skillet, or heavy frying pan over medium-high heat.

glossaryTerms.definition: The technique of spreading fat over a rolled dough round, folding it into thirds or a triangle, resting briefly, and rolling again. Each fold traps layers of fat between sheets of dough, which separate when cooked on the griddle to give the characteristic flaky texture.

content.text: The flakiness of a paratha comes from

: rolling the dough thin, spreading ghee across it, folding it up, resting for a few minutes, then rolling again. Wholemeal flour (atta) gives a softer, more flavourful result than plain flour and is the traditional choice.

items.prepNote: or half wholemeal, half plain flour
melted, for spreading and cooking; or unsalted butter

content.text: Combine the flour and salt. Add the warm water gradually, mixing to form a soft, smooth dough. Knead for 5 minutes until pliable. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Divide into 6 equal balls (about 80 g each). Cover with a damp cloth.

Roll one dough ball into a circle of about 18 cm. Spread a thin layer of melted ghee across the whole surface. Fold the circle into thirds (like a letter) to make a long rectangle, then fold the rectangle in thirds again to make a small square.
Rest the folded square for 5 minutes, then roll out again to a circle of about 20 to 22 cm. The layers will be visible in the dough.
Heat the pan over medium-high heat. Place the paratha in the dry pan. Cook for about 1 minute until the bottom shows light brown spots.

Flip, brush the cooked side with a little ghee, and cook for a further 1 minute. Flip again, brush the second side, and cook for 30 seconds more until both sides are evenly browned and a few darker patches have appeared.
Stack cooked parathas under a cloth to keep them soft. They firm up quickly if left uncovered.
